notes: Event date: 18 September 1944, the day Eindhoven was liberated (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10a, pp. 542-545; the day of liberation is the day named for the mobilisation, not a separately dated hour of Horrocks's acceptance). Event definition: On the day of Eindhoven's liberation, Captain W. J. van Dijk of the OD mobilised about 1,000 stoottroepen (and about 700 border guards) in the city; the military commissioner, Major Verhoeff, told him that the Military Authority would itself handle the border guard and that he should place his six companies of stoottroepen at the disposal of XXX Corps. He did so, and after Prince Bernhard's intervention (Montgomery had no interest) Horrocks accepted the companies. De Jong still calls them "stoottroepen van de OD" at this point (p. 543, footnote 2); they are entered on the formal Stoottroepen unit because they were already organised as six companies and placed under a corps, and they are the Brabant nucleus of the BS Stoottroepen organised in the following days. Footnote 2: in the Eindhoven area these OD stoottroepen at first helped cover the flanks of XXX Corps. Event support: one source family (de Jong's official history, volume 10a, read directly in NIOD's page-tagged CC-BY edition; printed pages cited, paraphrase only). Location: Eindhoven, Noord-Brabant (existing place PL2596) with a precision of 3 km. current_activity: Borghouts is appointed commander of the Stoottroepen der BS south of the great rivers; the BS are split into Stoottroepen and Bewakingstroepen
notes: Event date: 22 September 1944 (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10a, pp. 561-563). Event definition: Major van Houten, not then knowing that the prince had already appointed van Kooten commander in South Limburg, appoints Borghouts commander of the Stoottroepen der Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten south of the great rivers (and Hoekstra acting commander of this military formation), and gives command of the Bewakingstroepen to van Dijk; the Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten are split into Stoottroepen (to fight shoulder to shoulder with the Allies) and Bewakingstroepen (guard duties behind the front and of the camps). Event support: one source family (de Jong's official history, volume 10a, read directly in NIOD's page-tagged CC-BY edition; printed pages cited, paraphrase only). Location: the appointment is dated but de Jong does not name the town of van Houten's act on this row; Eindhoven is used as a representative point because Borghouts was operating from Eindhoven in these days (he returned there on the evening of 21 September, p. 561, and issued a regulation there on 25 September, p. 770). Precision 10 km. Review (de Jong 10a-1 follow-up, branch dejong-10a1, 12 November 2026, approved by Scott): new row; old value none, new value this claim (confidence 0.3: one source family, the command change is dated, but the place of the appointment is not named (representative point at Eindhoven)).

notes: Event date: early May 1945, represented as 1 May (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10a, p. 757). Event definition: A return compiled in London by the department of war gives, for early May 1945, six battalions of Stoottroepen and two battalions of Bewakingstroepen; in the Stoottroepen about 4,000 men had by then been brought together (apart from the staff), and in the Bewakingstroepen about 1,500. De Jong warns that the Bewakingstroepen figures are too low (van Ojen has 13,000-14,000 at the end of December 1944 and about 16,000 in mid-January 1945; those figures are recorded in the private notes and are not used on this row), and that the reader may take it that there were more than 10,000 Bewakingstroepen in the liberated south and about 4,000 Stoottroepen (p. 758). Event support: one source family (de Jong's official history, volume 10a, read directly in NIOD's page-tagged CC-BY edition; printed pages cited, paraphrase only). Location: Southern Netherlands (liberated area), a representative point with a precision of 50 km (the vocabulary maximum; the liberated south is wider); de Jong gives the figure for the liberated south as a whole, not a town.
